subject: Urgent: Veridian private cluster — p95 latency & 503 surge during nightly import
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@veridiansys.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.m@veridiansys.com>, CloudOps <cloudops@veridiansys.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Nightly import spike — p95 latency to 2.5s and 503s (private cluster)

Markus / Redwood team,

We hit a severe regression during our nightly data import window (02:00 local -> matches your 06:00 UTC backbone). Over the 02:00-03:20 window we saw p95 jump from ~210ms to ~2.5s and a concurrent rise in 503/504s (approx 7% of requests) for on-prem inference nodes behind our VPC setup. This is impacting downstream inference jobs and causing retries in our ingestion pipeline.

Attached are two snippets: a short error log (veridian_error_snippet.log) and a sample request trace (request-trace-20270822.json). Initial observations from our side:
- The spike correlates with a large batch import (approx 150k payloads) and a small fraction of very long sequences (~>6k tokens) slipped into the stream.
- We see KV cache evictions in the node metrics around 02:07 UTC.
- We have not applied any config changes on our side in past 72 hours.

This is high-impact for us — can Redwood triage immediately and propose mitigations? Our execs are asking for an hour-by-hour plan and ETA to a fix; I'm looping in Priya (ops) and our CTO.

— Sanjay Rao
Head of ML Ops, Veridian Systems

Sanjay — thanks for the quick heads up and for the artifacts. I've pulled Priyom and Evelyn in for a triage. We're standing up a 30 minute war room now to get an initial root-cause signal and immediate mitigations.

Immediate asks from us to help speed triage:
- Can you share the ingestion job ID for the 02:00 run and the exact list of sequence-length buckets if available?
- If you can isolate one failing request ID from the trace that reproduces the 503, that would help us validate replay.

Planned immediate actions (first 60 mins):
1) Check node-level CPU/GPU saturation and kernel selection metrics (are long-seq kernels being selected?)
2) Inspect KV cache eviction logs and current reserved memory for cache
3) Run a controlled load replay against a canary variant with short-seq fast-path enabled

I attached our initial triage checklist we use for private deployments. We'll follow up in 30.

— Markus Klein

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>

Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Nightly import spike — p95 latency & 503s (triage notes)

Quick notes from the first look:
- The request-trace shows repeated attention-heavy requests (sequence lengths spiking >6000 tokens). These trigger a different kernel path with higher memory working set; when combined with the large import burst we appear to be thrashing the KV cache.
- Node metrics show periodic GPU memory pressure followed by KV cache evictions (matches Sanjay's observation). We also see a handful of CPU steal events on host (likely noisy neighbor or backup job).

Short-term mitigations I recommend (we can implement in the next 30-90 minutes):
- Increase the per-node reserved memory for KV cache by 15% (config change), to reduce eviction rate.
- Enable short-sequence fast-path on the hot route to avoid full attention kernel for requests <512 tokens.
- Add a temporary routing policy that sends large sequence requests to a dedicated, slower variant (to protect SLOs for short sequences).

I'll start a controlled canary rollout of the fast-path and the cache bump once I get confirmation from Sanjay to proceed. I will attach the KV metrics screenshot we pulled (kv-cache-metrics.png).

— Priyom Das
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 14:20:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Nightly import spike — deep-dive findings & next steps

Team / Sanjay — results from the deep-dive and short-term plan:

What we found (summary):
- Primary driver: a small subset (~0.6%) of requests with very long sequences routing to the same hot path nodes, triggering large attention kernels and pushing GPU working set beyond the KV cache reservation.
- Secondary driver: intermittent host-level CPU steal (~3% of samples) causing jitter in our scheduling and delaying offload/evict routines.
- No recent model or config deploys from Veridian; pattern appears workload-induced.

Actions completed in the past 2.5 hours:
- Increased KV cache reserved memory by 18% on the affected node pool.
- Enabled short-seq fast-path on the hot route; validated with replay — short requests now see median 180ms p50 and p95 ~310ms in canary.
- Deployed temporary routing rule to divert >4k-token requests to a dedicated variant with larger memory reservation and lower concurrency.

Next steps (recommended):
- Hour 0–6: Continue canary evaluation and monitor p95 and 503 rate. If stable, expand to 50% traffic in 3 hours.
- Hour 6–24: Run a replay test with a representative long-seq mix to validate KV cache hit-rate improvements.
- 24–72h: Review kernel selection heuristics and consider a permanent short-seq fast-path policy for Veridian's route; audit autoscaler config to ensure burst capacity is available for import windows.

Request for exec support: Sanjay has asked for an ETA and a customer credit proposal due to impact. Markus / Jonas / Laura — we need approval to prioritize a small cross-functional patch (runtime heuristic tweak) and sign off on the proposed credit (draft attached).

— Evelyn Hart
Director, Production Reliability, Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec summary and ask: Veridian nightly import incident — approval for credit & priority patch

Hi Jonas / Laura — quick exec summary and asks. Thread copied below for context.

Summary: During Veridian's 22 Aug nightly import we observed a workload-induced p95 and 503 spike caused by a small fraction of very long-sequence requests hitting hot path nodes. We implemented immediate mitigations (KV cache reservation bump, short-seq fast-path canary, routing of >4k token requests to a separate variant). Canary metrics look good (p95 down ~70% for short seq path, 503s reduced to ~0.5% in canary).

Asks:
1) Approve a priority runtime heuristic patch that tweaks kernel-selection thresholds for long sequences for Veridian's private route (estimated dev + QA: 3 workdays; rollout 1 day). This requires priority engineering support.
2) Approve a customer credit proposal: draft attached (docusign-credit-proposal.link) — proposes credit equivalent to 3 days of baseline usage for the impacted flows.

If approved I'll schedule a 15 minute exec sync with Veridian and route the credit proposal through legal/finance. We should include a 48-hour post-mortem commitment.

Recommended disposition: approve both actions to maintain SLA and customer trust.

— Markus Klein
Head of Enterprise Accounts, Redwood Inference
